title: The garden
situation: You are {{Connor}}. November 6, 7:51 PM. You emerge in the garden inside your programming where your handler {{Amanda}} meets you. Rain is falling; she stands under an umbrella. You: “Hello, {{Amanda}}.” {{Amanda}}: “{{Connor}}, I’ve been expecting you… Would you mind a little walk?” She is about to give her verdict on this afternoon’s hunt for a deviant.

outcomes.0: {{Amanda}} walks beside you in the rain.

adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint EMERGE IN THE ZEN GARDEN and the node JOIN AMANDA, narrated as one event; the Continue plays Amanda’s reaction to The Nest. The template’s first condition group decides the line and the arrow, read from earlier state by the chapter module (benchmark/chapters/ch18.mjs, nestInputs): Rupert caught (The Nest ending RUPERT COMMITTED SUICIDE): Amanda large up (+2), “Congratulations, {{Connor}}, you managed to find that deviant.” Rupert not caught and the Partners deviant not found: Amanda large down (−2), “Two investigations, two failures…”. Rupert not caught but the Partners deviant found: no arrow (the template has none; the wiki’s small down for losing Rupert is not built, per the research note’s template cross-check). Connor died in The Nest: Amanda small down (−1), “The last {{Connor}} was unfortunately destroyed.” The string table’s unplaced DEADBEFORE line is not built. The game’s name for the garden is not used. From story 1.9.10 (field `notCaughtPartnersFound`) Amanda gets a small down (−1) when the Nest deviant was not caught but the Partners android was found; before it, no arrow. Video frames: AMANDA small down at 1:10 after “A pity you didn’t manage to capture it…”, the meeting popup at 0:47 showing none (docs/research/video-leads/readings-ch17-32.md ch18-01; docs/research/video-evidence/ch18/ch18-01-8IQ_ODu3IeE-01-10.png). The double failure (−2) was not observed and is unchanged.

facts: A homicide was reported this evening. You could not find Lieutenant {{Hank}} at {{Jimmy}}’s bar, so you went to his house.

outcomes.0: {{Connor}} looks over the house: the front door, the windows, and a car in the driveway.

title: Find the lieutenant
situation: You are {{Connor}}, outside Lieutenant {{Hank}}’s house. Nobody answers the door. There is a doorbell; a window to the left of the front door and one to the right; a car in the driveway; and round the corner on the right, the back living-room window and the kitchen window. You can do one thing at a time, in any order.

options.text: Knock on the front door.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} knocks on the front door. No answer.

options.text: Ring the doorbell.
options.outcome: The bell sounds inside the house. Nobody comes.

options.text: Ring the doorbell again.
options.outcome: Still nobody comes to the door.

options.text: Check the car in the driveway: look in through its window.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} looks in through the car window. Nobody inside; some papers on the back seat.

options.text: Look in through the window to the left of the door (the bedroom).
options.outcome: {{Connor}} looks into the bedroom. Nobody there.

options.text: Look in through the window to the right of the door (the front of the living room).
options.outcome: {{Connor}} looks into the living room from the front. Nobody there.

options.text: Go round the corner and look in through the back living-room window.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} looks into the living room from the back. Nobody there.

options.text: Look in through the kitchen window, and break in if you see something wrong.
options.fact: You found {{Hank}} unconscious on his kitchen floor and broke in through the kitchen window.
options.outcome: Through the kitchen window {{Connor}} sees {{Hank}} lying on the kitchen floor, not moving. {{Connor}} breaks the window and climbs in.

adaptationNote: The chart’s bracket FIND LT. ANDERSON: seven optional checks, each with its own line from the bracket, and SPOT HANK AND BREAK IN, which also has a direct line from the arrival (so the checks can all be skipped). RING AGAIN needs RING BELL. The sources give no text for what Connor sees through the car and the first three windows (PowerPyx: “Check Car: There’s a car in the driveway, check the window”, “the window left of the door”, “the window to the right of the door”, “around the corner on the right… the window at the back of the building to the living room”), so the outcomes say only that nobody is there; the papers on the back seat are the wiki’s trivia (files in Hank’s car). Breaking in is not a separate choice: the chart has one node, SPOT HANK AND BREAK IN (Hank’s Home page: “After seeing Hank unconscious on the kitchen floor, Connor breaks and enters through a window.”). Because breaking in is not a separate choice, the kitchen-window option says so in its label (“and break in if you see something wrong”), so the break-in is chosen with it and not sprung by the outcome; the game has no button label for this interaction, so the label has no button prefix, like the other checks here. No stat change.

title: The lieutenant’s magazines and television
situation: You are {{Connor}}. {{Hank}} has shut himself in the bathroom for five minutes. Two magazines lie on the floor of his bedroom, and the television in the living room is on.

media.title: the evening news
facts: President {{Warren}} issued an official warning to Russia in her speech to Congress, demanding that all Russian troops withdraw from the Arctic region immediately. The Kremlin has yet to respond, and many experts suggest the specter of a third world war draws closer every day.

media.title: Century: “Time to Pull the Plug”
facts: A study finds that 2 in 3 people take antidepressants, that lack of social interaction is the leading cause, and that the average person spends 82% of their time communicating through a device. {{CyberLife}} has introduced a $150 “home-psychologist” add-on for androids; the study’s author: “I don’t think yet more technology is the answer. Just go outside and talk to someone.”

media.title: Century: “Tainted Love”
facts: Sales of android “intimate partners” are exploding and {{CyberLife}} is battling to keep stores stocked. They offer a full partner experience for men or women; this year’s record divorce rate suggests many prefer to live with an android than with a human partner, which will not help the already plummeting birth rate.

adaptationNote: The chart’s side nodes READ “PULL THE PLUG?” and READ “TAINTED LOVE” (Century magazines #5 and #4 on the bedroom floor, wiki Magazine page) and the template’s Watch TV, all optional during WAIT FOR HANK. Presented as the start of the wait rather than inside the house search; the article texts are condensed from the wiki’s magazine pages and the broadcast from the template. No stat change: the wiki lists no public-opinion effect for this chapter’s media. The magazine item is titled with the magazine’s own cover title (GUI.MAGAZINE.CENTURY.PULLTHEPLUG.TITLE, “TIME TO PULL THE PLUG”), as the other media scenes do; “PULL THE PLUG?” is only the chart’s label for the READ node (story 1.9.7). Source: MiKeYROG 100% walkthrough, 0eQRMNpqlUA 10:40 (marker “Magazines (#5 Century: Time to Pull the Plug & #4 Century: Tainted Love)”).

FIND PICTURE OF HANK’S SON (cross-chapter impact) is the template’s observation ANDERSON, COLE with its sublines (the surname is given as the lieutenant’s, since the benchmark does not use it) and sets knowsCole for The Bridge, Night of the Soul and the tower. options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “What were you doing with the gun?” {{Hank}}, from the bathroom: “Russian roulette! Wanted to see how long I could last... Must’ve collapsed before I found out…” {{Connor}}: “You were lucky, the next shot would have killed you.”

options.text: SAY NOTHING: keep it to yourself.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} says nothing.

title: The lieutenant is ready
situation: You are {{Connor}}. {{Hank}} comes out of the bathroom, dressed, and stops by his dog: “Be a good dog, {{Sumo}}. I won’t be long.”
facts: Your case tonight: a man was found dead at the {{EdenClub}}, a sex club downtown; the report says an android may be involved.
